div.l: This is þe pointe to speke shorte and plaine
That eueriche of you to shorte his wey
In þis viage shal tel tales twey
To Caunterbury wardis I mene it so
And homwardꝭes he shal tel oþer two
Of Auentours þat whilom hath be fall
And which of you bereth best of all
That is to say telleth in þis cas
Tales of best sentence and solace
Shal haue a souꝑper at our aller coste
Here in þis place sitting at this poste
Whan that we come a gayn̄ from Caunt̉erbury
And for to make you þe more mery
I will my self gladlich with you ride
At myn̄ own̄ cost and be youre gide
And who so wol my iugement deny
Shal pay al þat we spend bi þe wey
And if ye vouchesaue þat it be so
Tel me anon̄ withoute wordez mo
And I wil erly shape me þer for
Thies þyngꝭes wer graunted ⁊and oþes swor
With ful glad hert and praied him also
That he wold vouchesaue so todo
And þat he wold be oure gouernour
And of oure tales Iuge and reportour
And set a suꝑper at a certein price
And we wold ruled be at his device
In hie and lowe and thus be one assente
We ben̄ accorded to his Iugemente
And ther vpon the wyn was fet a none
We drank and to rest went ichone
Withoute ony lenger tarying
And on þe morow whan dai gan spring
Vp roose oure oost þat was oure kok
And gadered vs to gidre in a flok
And forth we riden litul more þan a paas
Vnto watering of seint Thomas
And þere oure oost began his horse arrest
And seid sirres herkeneth if you list
I wote youre forward and I shal you recorde
There are small "2"s written above each of "euensong and mornsong". MR take these as indicating transposition. If euensong and mornsong accorde
Late se now ho shal tel first his tale
As euer mote I drink wyn or ale
